posts.headline: TWFG Names Andy McGuire Chief Underwriting Officer to Accelerate Growth
posts.body: TWFG Inc. (NASDAQ: TWFG) appointed Andy McGuire as Chief Underwriting Officer on Feb. 17, 2026 to accelerate national growth and MGA expansion. McGuire brings extensive industry experience and leadership background that aligns with TWFG’s culture and growth objectives. The move signals TWFG’s commitment to scaling its insurance distribution platform across the country, particularly in the managing general agent (MGA) space. Investors responded positively to the leadership change, viewing it as a strategic step toward expanding market share in the competitive insurance sector.

posts.headline: Warner Bros. Discovery Files Proxy Statement for Netflix Merger Vote
posts.body: Warner Bros. Discovery, Inc. filed a definitive proxy statement with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Feb. 17, 2026, announcing a Special Meeting of Shareholders scheduled for March 20, 2026 to vote on the merger with Netflix. The proxy statement was first mailed to WBD stockholders on or around Feb. 17. The $82.7 billion transaction would see Netflix acquire Warner Bros. Entertainment, DC Comics/Studios, and HBO Max, while WBD’s global linear networks would be spun off. The filing marks a significant step toward completing what would be one of the largest media mergers in history.

posts.headline: Danaher to Acquire Masimo in $9.9 Billion Diagnostics Push
posts.body: Danaher Corporation (NYSE: DHR) agreed to acquire Masimo Corporation (NASDAQ: MASI) for $9.9 billion on Feb. 17, 2026, expanding into patient-monitoring devices outside its core diagnostics focus. Danaher will pay $180 per share in cash, representing a 40% premium to Masimo’s closing price. The acquisition of the pulse oximeter maker allows Danaher to strengthen its medical technology portfolio and gain a foothold in the medical supply business. The deal, expected to close in early 2026, underscores Danaher’s strategy of strategic bolt-on acquisitions to complement organic growth.

posts.headline: Empire State Realty Trust Renews Leases with TJ Maxx and JP Morgan Chase
posts.body: Empire State Realty Trust, Inc. (NYSE: ESRT) announced on Feb. 17, 2026 that it signed long-term renewal leases with TJ Maxx and JP Morgan Chase Bank for retail spaces totaling 68,120 square feet. The leases cover 46,437 square feet for TJ Maxx and 21,683 square feet for JP Morgan Chase at Empire State Realty’s flagship properties. The renewals demonstrate continued demand for premium retail space in Manhattan and provide stability to ESRT’s cash flow. The long-term commitments from these established tenants signal confidence in New York City’s retail market recovery.

posts.headline: urban-gro Completes Merger with Flash Sports and Media
posts.body: urban-gro, Inc. (NASDAQ: UGRO) completed its merger with Flash Sports and Media, Inc. on Feb. 17, 2026, providing shareholders with access to the rapidly evolving sports and media digital landscape. The transaction, first announced on Oct. 14, 2025, provides Flash shareholders with unregistered shares of urban-gro’s common stock and newly created non-voting preferred stock. Upon stockholder approval, the preferred stock will convert to common stock, with the total shares equaling Flash’s agreed equity valuation divided by $3.23, urban-gro’s closing price on Feb. 17. The merger expands urban-gro’s presence in the sports technology sector.

posts.headline: S&P 500 Edges Higher as Financial Stocks Offset Tech Weakness
posts.body: U.S. equity markets concluded a volatile session on Feb. 17, 2026 with major indexes managing to edge into positive territory despite significant intraday swings. The S&P 500 rose 0.1% to close at 6,843.22, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed 32.26 points, or 0.07%, settling at 49,533.19. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite lagged, shedding roughly 0.5% as investors grappled with evolving artificial intelligence impacts on software and IT services. Financial stocks provided support, offsetting continued weakness in the technology sector amid concerns about AI-driven disruption in software and IT services.
